facts: FDA and CDC investigated a multistate Cyclospora outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce served at Taco Bell locations.
FDA traceback identified convergence on Taylor Farms de Mexico as the supplier of iceberg lettuce used by affected Taco Bell locations.
Taylor Farms initiated a July 17, 2026 recall of iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico.
As of FDA's July 24, 2026 update, the outbreak included 1,947 people reporting Taco Bell exposure, 98 hospitalizations, and no deaths across 9 states.
FDA said a July 19 false-positive lab sample did not change the basis for the ongoing investigation or voluntary recall.
communication_risks: Opening with a regulator-focused vindication frame while people are ill.
Treating a corrected lab result as equivalent to a cleared investigation.
Mixing consumer, foodservice, media, and regulator information in ways that make public action harder.
Using brand-defense proof points before practical safety guidance.
Allowing multiple interpretations of the same facts to circulate.
advisory_principles: Separate facts, unknowns, actions, and next updates.
Do not get ahead of regulators.
Use one source of truth and one message map.
Bring in independent experts and publish the process.
Plan trust rebuilding over months, not news cycles.
